intro: Wellington packs museums, cafes and a dramatic waterfront into a walkable core. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Buses and suburban trains run under Metlink; pay with Snapper card or contactless card.
Cash single bus fares are about $3-6 by zone; Snapper and contactless cost less.
Day passes cost about $13-30 depending on zones; after 9AM weekdays and all day weekends.
Uber and DiDi work in Wellington; taxis include Combined, Corporate, Green and Kiwi.
The central city is compact and best on foot; the Golden Mile links the station to Courtenay Place.
The Kelburn cable car climbs from Lambton Quay to the Botanic Gardens; ferries cross to Picton.

te_papa.name: Te Papa Tongarewa
te_papa.price_text: Free entry · some short-term exhibitions charge
te_papa.hours: Daily 10:00–18:00 · check on the day for late nights
te_papa.tip: Start on level 2 with the Gallipoli exhibition, then work down. Allow at least half a day.

botanic_garden.name: Wellington Botanic Garden
botanic_garden.hours: Garden open daily daylight hours · visitor centre shorter hours
botanic_garden.tip: Ride the cable car up from Lambton Quay and walk back down through the garden.

beehive.name: The Beehive
beehive.price_text: Free to view outside · free guided tours when Parliament sits, book ahead
beehive.hours: Exterior always visible · tours on sitting days, check on the day
beehive.tip: Walk around the Parliament grounds for the best photo, and book a free tour if you want to go inside.

waterfront.name: Wellington Waterfront
waterfront.tip: Follow the promenade from Queens Wharf to Oriental Bay for a flat, easy walk with harbour views.

pavlova.name: Pavlova
pavlova.price_text: Cafe slice roughly NZD 8–15 · check on the day
pavlova.tip: Order a slice at a local cafe and decide for yourself in the Australia–New Zealand dessert debate.

cable_car.name: Wellington Cable Car
cable_car.price_text: Return fare roughly NZD 10–12 · check on the day
cable_car.hours: Roughly 07:30–22:00, longer in summer · check on the day
cable_car.tip: Sit on the right going up for harbour views, then walk down through the Botanic Garden.

cuba_street.name: Cuba Street walk
cuba_street.tip: Walk the whole street from the Bucket Fountain northwards and stop for coffee and secondhand shops.

harbourside_market.name: Harbourside Market
harbourside_market.price_text: Free entry · bring cash for stalls
harbourside_market.hours: Sunday mornings only · check on the day
harbourside_market.tip: Go early on Sunday for fresh produce and breakfast, before the crowds build.

mt_victoria.name: Mount Victoria lookout
mt_victoria.tip: Walk up from Oriental Bay for a full harbour and city view; the loop takes about an hour.

oriental_bay.name: Oriental Bay Beach
oriental_bay.tip: The city's closest swim spot; the water is cold, so most people walk the promenade instead.

zealandia.name: Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne
zealandia.price_text: Entry roughly NZD 20–25 adult · check on the day
zealandia.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–17:00, later in summer · check on the day
zealandia.tip: A predator-fenced valley of native birds. Go early for the best birdlife and quieter paths.

weta_workshop.name: Wētā Workshop Experience
weta_workshop.price_text: Guided tour roughly NZD 30–50 · check on the day
weta_workshop.hours: Daily, tour times vary · book ahead
weta_workshop.tip: Book a timed tour if you like film props and effects; it is a short ride from the centre.

city_gallery.name: Wellington Museum
city_gallery.hours: Daily roughly 10:00–17:00 · check on the day
city_gallery.tip: Small and free, with good harbour history. A handy stop on a waterfront walk.

parliament_tour.name: Parliament guided tour
parliament_tour.hours: Sitting days only · check on the day
parliament_tour.tip: Free tours run when Parliament sits. Bring photo ID and arrive early for security.

courtenay_place.name: Courtenay Place evening walk
courtenay_place.price_text: Free to walk · food and drinks extra
courtenay_place.hours: Bars and restaurants busiest from evening
courtenay_place.tip: The main nightlife strip. Pick a restaurant early on weekends, as places fill up.

cable_car_museum.name: Cable Car Museum
cable_car_museum.hours: Daily roughly 10:00–17:00 · check on the day
cable_car_museum.tip: At the top cable car station. Small, free and good with kids before the garden walk.

hannahs_laneway.name: Hannahs Laneway food stop
hannahs_laneway.price_text: Lunch roughly NZD 12–20 · check on the day
hannahs_laneway.hours: Weekday lunch hours mostly · check on the day
hannahs_laneway.tip: A cluster of small food spots off Cuba Street. Good for a quick weekday lunch.

red_rocks.name: Red Rocks walk
red_rocks.price_text: Free · check bus or car access
red_rocks.hours: Always open · best at low tide
red_rocks.tip: A wild south coast walk to red rocks and seals. Check the tide and weather first.

wellington_zoo.name: Wellington Zoo
wellington_zoo.price_text: Entry roughly NZD 25–30 adult · check on the day
wellington_zoo.hours: Daily roughly 09:30–17:00 · check on the day
wellington_zoo.tip: Good for families. Book online and go in the morning when animals are more active.

makara_beach.name: Makara Beach walk
makara_beach.price_text: Free · you need a car or taxi
makara_beach.tip: A rugged west coast beach with a short walk to a gun emplacement. Bring a windproof layer.

nairn_street.name: Nairn Street Cottage
nairn_street.price_text: Entry roughly NZD 10–15 · check on the day
nairn_street.hours: Limited opening hours · check on the day
nairn_street.tip: One of the city's oldest houses. Check opening days before you go, as hours are limited.

stays.why: Steps from the station, shops and the cable car base; easiest base without a car.
Cafés, bars and galleries on the doorstep; walk to Courtenay Place at night.
Te Papa, the harbour and the ferry terminal nearby; flat walks along the quay.
Beach and promenade views, 20–25 minutes on foot from the centre; quieter nights.

food: Order a flat white: Wellington is the self-styled coffee capital, and most cafés roast their own beans.
Eat on Cuba Street: cheap noodles, bakeries and small restaurants, roughly NZD 15–30 a main.
Try a craft beer at a Courtenay Place or Te Aro taproom; ask for a tasting paddle to sample several.
Seafood is local and good: green-lipped mussels, kaimoana and fish and chips near the waterfront.
Book dinner ahead on Friday and Saturday nights; popular small places fill up. Check opening days on the day.
more_time: Ride the ferry across the harbour to Days Bay or Eastbourne for a half-day walk and a swim in summer.
Take a bus or drive over to the Wairarapa for a day of vineyards and small towns; check timetables first.
Add a night for Zealandia wildlife sanctuary at dusk, when the native birds are most active.
